title: Control charts
subtitle: A factory cannot inspect every item — but it can watch the average and notice the moment the process drifts.

var.title: Two kinds of variation
var.body: Every process varies. Common-cause variation is the steady random noise of a healthy process; special-cause variation comes from something specific (worn tool, new supplier). Statistical quality control (SQC) separates the two so we act only on real changes.

xbar.title: The X̄ chart
xbar.body: Take small samples (size n) regularly and plot each sample mean. Centre line = grand mean X̿. Control limits sit three standard errors away: UCL, LCL = X̿ ± 3σ/√n (or X̿ ± A₂R̄ from tabulated constants). Because P(|Z| ≤ 3) = 0.9973, a healthy process almost never crosses them by chance: about 1 false alarm in 370.
xbar.steps: Grand mean 50, σ = 4, n = 4. SE = 4/√4. Limits = 50 ± 3·2.

rules.title: Signals beyond one point
rules.body: A single point outside the limits is one signal. Others: 7 points in a row on one side of the centre line, 6 steadily rising, 2 of 3 beyond 2σ. Each pattern is unlikely under pure noise, so it flags a shift earlier than waiting for the limit.

p.title: Charts for attributes
p.body: For defective fractions use the p-chart: centre p̄, limits p̄ ± 3√(p̄(1 − p̄)/n). For defects per unit use the c-chart: c̄ ± 3√c̄ (Poisson). Lower limits below zero are set to zero.

cap.title: Process capability
cap.body: Control asks “is it stable?”; capability asks “does it meet the spec?” Cp = (USL − LSL)/6σ. Cp ≥ 1.33 is comfortable; Cp = 1 leaves 0.27 % out of spec. Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/3σ also penalises an off-centre mean.
cap.steps: Spec 40–60, σ = 2.5: 6σ = 15. So Cp = 1.33 if the mean is centred.

acc.title: Acceptance sampling
acc.body: A single-sampling plan (n, c) inspects n items from a lot and accepts if at most c are defective. The operating-characteristic curve plots P(accept) against the lot defect rate — computed with the binomial (or Poisson). Producer’s risk α rejects a good lot; consumer’s risk β accepts a bad one.
